problem: Which value of $z$ satisfies the equation $\frac{2z-1}{6z}=\frac{3z-1}{3z}+\frac{z-1}{6z}?$

feedback.worked_solution:
We note that $a=0$ cannot be a solution since division by $0$ is undefined. 

The equation has the denominators $a$ and $3a.$ So first, we find the least common multiple (or $\text{LCM}$) of the denominators. We find that

$$
\text{LCM}(a,3a)=3a.
$$

So, we multiply both sides of the equation by $3a,$ and simplify: 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{a+3}{3a} & =\frac{a-1}{a}+2 \\ 3a\cdot (\frac{a+3}{3a}) & =3a\cdot (\frac{a-1}{a}+2) \\ 3a\cdot \frac{a+3}{3a} & =3a\cdot \frac{a-1}{a}+3a\cdot 2 \\ \cancel{3a}\cdot \frac{a+3}{\cancel{3a}} & =3\cancel{a}\cdot \frac{a-1}{\cancel{a}}+6a \\ a+3 & =3(a-1)+6a\end{aligned}
$$

We now have a linear equation in $a,$ and we can solve this using the addition and multiplication principles:

$$
\begin{aligned}a+3 & =3(a-1)+6a \\ a+3 & =9a-3 \\ 9a-a & =3+3 \\ 8a & =6 \\ a & =\frac{3}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we recall that we cannot allow $a=0$ as a solution. But since $a=\frac{3}{4}\ne 0,$ we conclude that the solution is $a=\frac{3}{4}.$
